items.title: VisionQuest is what happens when AI really goes rogue
items.summary:
In Marvel's VisionQuest, a superpowered robot tries to better understand humanity by getting lost in elaborate, digital daydreams in which he and other artificial intelligence-powered beings live together in a home. The series is deeply fantastical, yet it plays with some of the ideas that have come to dominate the conversation about real-world generative artificial intelligence, exploring whether we should look at thinking machines as people and if AI truly poses the kind of existential danger that should keep us up at night. It's also a reminder how aggressively Silicon Valley has used the trappings of science fiction to sell us on its AI  …

items.title: The Super Mouse puts a touchscreen macro pad under your hand
items.summary:
A company called Arctic Fox Technologies has announced a new multifunction mouse that forgoes a myriad of customizable shortcut buttons peppered across its surface for a compact touchscreen sitting beneath your hand. The Super Mouse may not prioritize ergonomics with its boxy design, but it can replace other peripherals on your desk, like a trackpad, macro pad, or streaming controller. If you're faster at typing on your phone, the Super Mouse could potentially even replace a full-size keyboard with a smartphone-sized alternative that even includes swipe typing.
The Super Mouse is now available for preorder through a Kickstarter crowdfunding …

items.title: Anthropic’s elaborate plan to keep Wall Street at bay
items.summary:
Anthropic cofounder and CEO Dario Amodei. | Bloomberg via Getty Images	

Anthropic wants to have it both ways. With its impending IPO, it wants to tap the vast riches of the public markets and insists it doesn't want to compromise its core mission of developing AI safely and for the benefit of humanity. But greater model capabilities bring greater risks, and shareholders eager for returns may have little patience for costly safety measures that slow products on their way to market.
Sam Altman, the CEO of Anthropic's archrival, OpenAI, has cited investor pressures as one reason the company is not pursuing an IPO this year. Anthropic hopes it can resist investor pressures with a mind-boggling governance structure.

items.title: Meta’s $25 billion legal loss just put blood in the water
items.summary:
When attorneys general from across the US announced a $17 billion settlement with Meta this summer, the sum was unprecedented. But a ruling last week by a New Mexico judge blew that number out of the water. The judge ordered Meta to pay $25 billion to resolve claims that Meta misled users around the 2018 Cambridge Analytica scandal and related incidents. Similar claims were resolved by the settlement with most other states. The outcome raised an obvious question: Should these states have asked for more?
The answer depends on a mix of factors, including whether the $25 billion order stands up to Meta's legal challenges. Meta's chief legal of …

Firefox’s Smart Window adds AI form filling and webpage monitoring
items.summary:
Mozilla is updating Smart Window - Firefox's AI-powered browsing experience - with a new feature that can help you fill out online forms based on your open tabs. As an example, Mozilla says Smart Window can pull information from your online portfolio or LinkedIn page to paste your work history into a job application.
You can try out this feature by clicking into a form with at least four text fields. From there, you'll see an option to "Fill from sources," which will show all of the tabs Firefox will draw from. Google’s next Genie AI model generates more realistic experiences
items.summary:
Google announced today its Genie 4 world model for generating interactive experiences using AI. The company says the model has four main updates: It allows for more realistic worlds, lets users update an experience in real time with a natural language prompt, can generate audio, and uses Gemini 3.8 Flash under the hood to help with its simulations. It also can create experiences that are about two minutes long, up from one minute for the previous Genie 3 model.

items.title: My favorite robot vacuum just got quieter, and more expensive
items.summary:
The Matic Serene looks identical to the current Matic but the company claims its hardware improvements make it much quieter. | Image: Matic	

Matic, the company behind my favorite robot vacuum, is launching its first new model since its 2023 debut: the Matic Serene. The new robotic floor cleaner has one key upgrade: noise reduction. With a promised output of just 52 decibels at its highest suction level, the Serene claims to be about as quiet as a running refrigerator. It costs $1,695, $200 more than the original Matic's current price, and is available now. The good news is the company is offering an upgrade path for existing Matic owners.
The Serene targets people "who are extremely noise sensitive," cofounder and president Mehul Nariyawala tells The Verge. But beyond no …

items.title: Apple’s latest AirTag is the cheapest it’s ever been
items.summary:
Thanksgiving is less than a month away, so now’s a good time to start preparing before the rush. Fortunately, Apple’s latest AirTag can help you keep tabs on your luggage and other belongings amid the holiday chaos, and it’s currently down to an all-time low of $23 ($6 off) at Amazon and Walmart.
Apple AirTag (second-gen)

Where to Buy:

 $29 $23 at Amazon
 $29 $23 at Walmart

If you own an iPhone, the second-gen AirTag is the best Bluetooth tracker you can buy. That’s largely due to Apple’s ultra-wideband chip, which enables Precision Finding and guides you to an object’s exact location with on-screen arrows, vibrations, and sounds. The second-gen model can also help you find things faster than the prior generation, as it lets you pick up those directional cues from up to 50 percent farther (it also offers greater Bluetooth range). In our tests, that meant faster connections and better performance across multiple floors, which could come in handy if you’ve left something behind in a hotel. You can even follow directions on an Apple Watch Series 9 or later, making it possible to track down your stuff without pulling out your phone.
The latest AirTag offers a few other perks for travelers, too. You can share it with up to five other people, which is handy if you’re traveling with family members. If your suitcase goes missing, you can also temporarily share its location with participating airlines, including both United and Delta. That means if your suitcase gets lost, airline staff can see its reported location, which can make it easier to track down and return to you. More conveniently, it runs on a replaceable CR2032 battery designed to last more than a year, so you won’t have to worry about charging it before every trip.
Read our AirTag (second-gen) review.

Three more Verge-approved deals
Cricut’s Joy 2 Plus Ultimate Bundle is on sale for $159 ($50 off) at Amazon, which is the second-best price we’ve seen for this particular bundle. The small cutting machine is probably the funnest gadget I’ve tested this year, one that makes it relatively easy for beginners to create personalized cards, stickers, labels, iron-on designs, and other projects. The bundle also includes a mini heat press, tools, and enough supplies to make up to 75 projects, so you can get started right out of the box. Read my hands-on impressions.
Ring’s latest Battery Doorbell 2K is available from Amazon, Target, and Ring for $44.99 ($55 off), which is just $5 shy of its all-time low. The wireless doorbell offers sharp 2K video with a 140-degree horizontal and vertical field of view, making it easier to see visitors and packages left at your door. It also features night vision to keep tabs on trick-or-treaters after dark, two-way audio to chat with visitors, and motion detection that alerts you when someone’s at your door.
You can now pick up N Edition of 8Bitdo’s Retro Mechanical Keyboard on Amazon for $50.99 ($49 off), which marks its best price to date. Designed to resemble Nintendo’s original NES controller, the tenkeyless mechanical board features hot-swappable switches and a pair of large “Super Buttons,” which you can program to launch apps, trigger keyboard shortcuts, and perform other tasks.
